newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia labour disputes drop in January.
newsitem.headline: Australia labour disputes drop in January.

text.p: Austraian labour disputes fell in January to 30 disputes and 23,300 lost working days, from 49 disputes and 27,600 lost days in December, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.
More than half the days lost in January, or 13,600, were in the construction industry, the bureau said.
The sector lost 1,200 working days in December.
But the total number of days lost in the month was the lowest since 11,000 in December 1995.
Working days lost in the year to January jumped 373,600 to 928,100 from 554,500 in the year to January, 1996.

Construction was again the worst-hit sector, accounting for 322,900 of the working days lost through the 12 months (up from 53,500), followed by education, health and community services, with 249,200 (from 71,500) and coal mining with 161,800
The major cause of all industrial rows was managerial policy, accounting for 46 percent of working days lost over the year to January, the bureau said.
Wage disputes accounted for 26 percent of days lost.

Western Australia state recorded the largest number of lost working days in January -- 15,300, compared with none in December -- and New South Wales the largest number over the 12 months -- 387,300, compared with 113,500 in the previous 12 months.
